title: TMTG's market-moving 'truths' API and Truth+
summary: TMTG did announce 'Truth API' on July 16, 2026. It is a paid, real-time licensed feed of 'the platform's most market-moving Truths', and interim CEO Kevin McGurn said 'Markets already move on Truth Social posts.' The FT, via Reuters, reported pricing of up to $100,000 a month, and TMTG later confirmed a $60K-$100K range and more than 10 customer agreements. Truth+ and its 'non-woke' Patriot Package are real, but they launched in 2024-2025, not alongside the API. TMTG also disputes that the feed gives 'early' access rather than faster delivery.

sub_claims.statement: TMTG announced a paid API offering a real-time feed of the platform's most market-moving truths.
sub_claims.finding: Truth API was announced July 16, 2026 (GlobeNewswire) and went live August 1, 2026. The release quotes McGurn: it 'delivers a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform's most market-moving Truths.' The feed covers the 10 most influential accounts, reportedly including Trump's, plus an archive back to 2022. It is aimed at HFT and algorithmic trading firms.

sub_claims.statement: Interim CEO Kevin McGurn said 'markets already move on Truth Social posts.'
sub_claims.finding: Multiple outlets quote McGurn saying exactly this at the announcement. He became interim CEO on about April 21-22, 2026, when Devin Nunes stepped down.

sub_claims.statement: The company is reportedly charging $100,000 a month and has multiple buyers.
sub_claims.finding: On July 17, 2026, the FT reported (Reuters syndicated it without independent verification) that TMTG pitched up to $100,000 a month, or about $60,000 a month on a three-year deal. On its August 2026 earnings call, TMTG said it had signed more than 10 customer agreements at $60K-$100K a month, mostly with HFT firms. Reuters sources named Bloomberg, Susquehanna and Jump Trading as customers. $100K is the top of the range.

sub_claims.statement: You can pay to get the president's market-moving truths early, or at least in real time.
sub_claims.finding: The feed is a paid, low-latency, machine-readable delivery of posts. TMTG says all users see posts at the same time and the feed is only 'fractionally faster.' Critics, including Warren and Schiff and the Healthy Markets Association, call it a two-tiered market. 'Real time / faster' is documented. Pre-publication 'early' access is not established.

sub_claims.statement: TMTG also announced Truth+, a subscription streaming service offering Patriot packages with non-woke movies.
sub_claims.finding: The product is real. Truth+ (formerly TMTG+) debuted in 2024 and came to Roku in March 2025, marketed as 'the singular option for non-woke TV.' It launched globally on July 7, 2025. The $9.99 Patriot Package tier entered beta in July 2025, and on Aug 7, 2025 the Great American Media catalogue was added, pitched as 'non-woke entertainment.' None of this was announced alongside the July 2026 API, as the video's 'meanwhile' implies.

corrections: The $100,000/month figure is the top of a $60,000-$100,000 range. The FT first reported it from anonymous sources, and TMTG confirmed the range on its August 2026 earnings call.
'Multiple buyers' understates it: TMTG claims more than 10 customer agreements, and Reuters named Bloomberg, Susquehanna and Jump Trading.
Truth+ and its Patriot Package were not announced alongside the API. Truth+ dates to 2024, the Patriot Package to July 2025 and the non-woke film catalogue to August 2025.
'Early' access is disputed. TMTG says posts are public to all at the same moment and the API only speeds up machine delivery.
denials_and_context: TMTG calls Truth API an 'industry-standard' data product with significant demand and says it offers only 'fractionally faster' access to public posts. It accused Senate Democrats of misrepresenting the service. The White House referred questions to TMTG.
Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Adam Schiff asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins on July 28-29, 2026 to investigate. The SEC acknowledged receipt and declined to comment further. No opened probe was found.
Trump's revocable trust is TMTG's largest shareholder (about 41% per Reuters and Fortune citing filings), so feed revenue benefits him indirectly.
The 'markets already move' premise holds only for some posts. A JPMorgan analysis, reported by Axios in July 2026, found most Trump posts no longer move bond markets.
TMTG is heavily loss-making (about $3.7M revenue and a $712M net loss for 2025), and McGurn said only 'modest' API revenue had been recognized.
